title: What can help children with hearing loss or deafness
intro: Hearing is essential for learning to speak and for development, so early detection and support for children with hearing loss matter greatly. Many effective options exist, from hearing aids to cochlear implants, speech therapy and sign language, and families are supported by specialist teams.

sections.heading: Early detection
paragraphs: In many countries newborns have a hearing screening in the first days of life. Parents should also watch for signs later, such as not reacting to loud sounds, delayed speech, not responding to their name or turning the television up. Any concern should lead to a hearing test by a children's ear specialist or paediatric audiologist, without waiting.

sections.heading: Causes
paragraphs: Causes include genetic factors, infections during pregnancy such as cytomegalovirus, premature birth, jaundice, meningitis, ear infections with fluid behind the eardrum, and noise exposure. Temporary conductive loss from glue ear is common and often improves with time or small ear tubes. Permanent loss involves the inner ear or hearing nerve.

sections.heading: Hearing aids and implants
paragraphs: Hearing aids can be fitted from a few weeks of age and are adjusted as the child grows. When aids give too little benefit in severe or profound loss, a cochlear implant may be offered, ideally at a young age. Bone conduction devices help children whose outer or middle ear is not formed normally. Regular checks keep devices working well.

sections.heading: Language and communication
paragraphs: Speech and language therapy, listening training and early intervention programmes support development. Some families choose sign language, spoken language or both, and bilingual approaches are possible. Learning is best when parents are involved from the start, talking, reading and playing together with face-to-face contact.

sections.heading: School and wellbeing
paragraphs: Support at school can include seating near the teacher, assistive listening systems, captioning and specialist teachers. Contact with other families and deaf adults helps children develop identity and confidence. Watch for tiredness, frustration or bullying, and ask for help early.

examples.title: Responding to a concern
examples.text: Imagine your toddler rarely reacts to sounds and speaks few words. You could ask your paediatrician for a referral for a hearing test without waiting.

examples.title: Supporting at home
examples.text: Suppose your child has new hearing aids. You might make sure they are worn daily, check batteries and talk face to face in quiet settings.
